A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 22-17: APPROVAL OF AN UPDATE TO THE CITY’S
  PUBLIC FACILITIES IMPACT FEE PROGRAM AND CONSIDERATION OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 2435 UPDATING THE CITY’S PUBLIC FACILITIES IMPACT FEE
  SCHEDULE AND ORDINANCE NO. 726 AMENDING CHAPTER 17.74 (PUBLIC
  FACILITIES FEES) OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE.

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Adopt Resolution No. 2435; 5) Introduce Ordinance
  No. 726 for first reading and 6) Continue the public hearing to the next City Council
  meeting for second reading and adoptions of Ordinance No. 726.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired about the possibility of adding an impact fee
  related to stormwater impacts. In response, Planning Director Wahba stated that
  stormwater issues are addressed through other mechanisms, specifically through LID
  (Low Impact Development) requirements. City Attorney Davis commented that
  stormwater related matters would usually be addressed as an assessment rather that a
  development impact fee.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN inquired as to the ability to the waive fees specifically
  for projects that are designed to help the City in meeting the State housing mandates.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a provision in the ordinance for the fees to
  be waived. City Attorney Davis clarified that the fees could be reduced under specific
  circumstances; but if the fee is waived, it could trigger prevailing wage requirements for
  the project.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved to open the public hearing. Hearing no
  objection, Mayor Mitchell so ordered and called for public comment. Hearing none, the
  public hearing was continued.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 23, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2435 UPDATING THE
  CITY’S PUBLIC FACILITIES IMPACT FEE SCHEDULE

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None.

  City Manager Prichard read the resolution by title.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 726 AMENDING
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 17.74 (PUBLIC
  FACILITIES FEES), CONDUCTED FIRST READING BY TITLE AND
  SCHEDULED SECOND READING AND ADOPTION FOR THE NEXT REGULAR
  MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None.

  City Manager Prichard read the ordinance by title.

NEW BUSINESS

Mayor Mitchell stated that in recognition of the fact that there are members of the audience present
to address item C, the item will be taken out of order. Hearing no objection, she so ordered.

*C.  APPROVAL OF SECOND AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH TRIPEPI SMITH

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve an Amendment to the Professional
  Services Agreement with Tripepi Smith for ongoing service in an amount of $1,942.50 per
  month beginning May 1, 2019.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and
  reviewed a PowerPoint presentation highlighting the projects and services that Tripepi
  Smith has provide over the last two years.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that the transfer of skills between Tripepi
  Smith and City staff is very encouraging.

  In response to Councilmember Huff’s inquiry regarding the City’s need for continued
  services, Assistant to the City Manager Davis explained that the services provided by
  Tripepi Smith will augment the City’s community outreach program to keep it at the level
  that has been achieved. She also commented that Tripepi Smith provides certain talent
  and expertise that City doesn’t currently have on staff, specifically – graphic design,
  analytics review and social media monitoring.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
APRIL 23, 2019
   In response to Councilmember Huff, Assistant to the City Manager Davis commented that
  the contract does not have a specific end date but will be reviewed each year and Council
  will be provide a review of the services provided.

  Also in response to Councilmember Huff, John Barilone with Tripepi Smith explained that
  the Community Round-up events will be a town hall type meeting to provided an
  opportunity for enhanced community engagement and give residents an opportunity to
  ask questions and gain information about the City.

  COUNCILMEMBER HUFF encouraged staff to continue to try to make progress in taking
  on these tasks.

  Ryder Smith commented that his firm has enjoyed working with the City and staff has
  been willing to listen and learn. He stated that in addition to the services provided, Tripepi
  Smith provided additional valued added services in being able to share insights from their
  experience of working with 40 cities and share best practices with the City.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that from a strategic marketing and data
  analytics perspective Tripepi Smith’s services have been very valuable.

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that she is supportive of continuing where the expertise
  does not exist with staff. She further commented that hiring a staff member with this type
  of expertise would far exceed the contract amount.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that this is what the contract cities model
  provides – expertise in a specific areas outside of the administrative function of staff at a
  reduced cost as compared to hiring a staff person. He stated that although staff is learning
  from this experience, he suspects there will always be a need for certain services outside
  the administrative function.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TRIPEPI SMITH FOR
  ONGOING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,942.50 PER MONTH
  BEGINNING MAY 1, 2019.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  None

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE FY 2019-20 STREET RESURFACING
  PROJECT – PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached plans, specifications and
  bid documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the FY 2019-20 Street Resurfacing
  Project on Palos Verdes Drive North.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ inquired as to the impact the Cal Water Project on Palos
  Verdes Drive North (PVDN) will have on this project, specifically in the areas that call for
  the project to join already resurfaced pavement. She wanted to ensure that both paving
  projects would be done to the City’s specifications.

  Discussion ensued concerning the paving on PVDN related to the Cal Water project and
  how it will impact the City’s 2019-20 street resurfacing project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that staff will work with Cal Water to ensure
  that when the street resurfacing related to the Cal Water project is finalized it meets the
  City’s expectations.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS AND BID
  DOCUMENTS; AND AUTHORIZE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE FY
  2019-20 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 725 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
